messages:
mike: Saw a sharp p99 tail during a customer burst tonight. p95 stable but p99 jumped ~130ms -> ~510ms for ~8m after autoscale. Initial traces point at KV misses + kernel compile/fallback on new nodes.

deploy-bot: Autoscaler event: added=4, pool=low-latency, reason=burst

mike: Paste from filtered trace: 
```
2026-03-14T02:11:23Z req=xyz seq=1024 batch=1 kernel=opt_gemm -> compile_cache_miss -> fallback=generic_matmul
2026-03-14T02:11:23Z kv: miss prefix=a1b2c3 (cold)
2026-03-14T02:11:23Z compile: kernel opt_gemm compile_time=95ms
2026-03-14T02:11:23Z end_to_end=512ms
```

irina: That compile_cache_miss line looks like new behavior we didn't see earlier. Sounds JIT/compile on first use. New nodes have empty kernel cache.

ben: Also noticed a flood of microbatch=1 requests right after scale-up. So each request pays full compile + KV miss. Bad combo.

sam: Why did selector go opt_gemm then fallback? Selector should probe earlier and decide against expensive kernel when node is fresh. Maybe prober sample size / policy is too aggressive.

mike: My working theory: selector uses historical seq_len distribution (long sequences predominant) so it prefers opt_gemm. On fresh nodes kernel cache miss triggers compile; compile latency + KV miss produce the tail. Two levers: reduce prober optimism for fresh nodes, or pre-warm kernels.

irina: Mitigations we can try quickly:
- Add kernel_preload hook in node bootstrap to background-load top-n kernels
- Set default.microbatch=4 for newly provisioned workers for first 2 minutes to amortize costs
- Increase prober cost threshold so fresh nodes prefer generic fallback until compile_time metric is low

ben: I can add a bootstrap flag `--bootstrap-hooks=kernel_preload` and a job that runs `rbw kernel-load --model=raven-3b --kernels=top2` during provisioning.

sam: I'll add runtime.metrics: `runtime.kernel.compile_time` histogram and `runtime.kernel.compile_cache_miss` counter with node and kernel tags. That'll let us see how often and how long compiles take.

mike: Quick local A/B: microbatch=1 p99 ~520ms; microbatch=4 p99 ~220ms, p95 moved 85->115ms. So batching cuts peak but costs small p95 bump. Customer SLO might accept the trade.

irina: Proposal: canary on 10% of new nodes with two changes: kernel_preload enabled + default.microbatch=4 for first 120s. Record compile_time and kv_miss_rate.

mike: I'll open a small infra PR and a perf dashboard tile. Ops needs to allow kernel-load during bootstrap. @ben want to own the PR? @sam will add metrics and dashboards.

ben: Taking PR. Will gate bootstrap kernel_preload behind account opt-in for now and add a feature flag so rollback is easy.

sam: Metric changes: adding histogram + count. Will also emit `runtime.kv.prefix_miss_rate{node,pool}`.

mike: If canary still shows bad p99 we'll implement sticky fallback: for first N requests on a fresh node force selector to choose generic kernels (no opt_gemm) until compile cache has warm hits. Also consider a tiny synthetic warmup call during node join that touches popular prefixes.

irina: Add runbook steps for oncall: 1) force microbatch=4 on affected pool, 2) enable bootstrap kernel_preload on pool, 3) slow down scale-up settings / increase node startup delay. Post to #eng-oncall when canary starts.

mike: Filed infra ticket: https://redwood.internal/p/infra/9832 "burst: autoscaler bootstrap kernel preload + microbatch canary" — will link PRs and dashboards.

ben: Canary scheduled tomorrow 09:00 UTC. Will report metrics back (p95/p99, compile_time, kv_miss_rate).

sam: Note: microbatch change affects throughput and per-token accounting. Coordinate with product/billing before wide rollout.

mike: Thanks all, drafting the PR + runbook now :thumbsup:
